'''Cynthia "Cyndie" Anne Maryanoff'''  ([[née]] Milewski; born November 27, 1949) is an American organic and materials [[chemist]].  Among other awards, she received the 2015 [[Perkin Medal]] for outstanding work in applied chemistry in the U.S.A.

==Education==
Cynthia Anne Milewski was born on November 27, 1949, in [[Shenandoah, Pennsylvania]].<ref name=Kay>{{cite book|editor-last1=Kay|editor-first1=Ernest|title=International who's who of professional and business women|date=1989|publisher=International Biographical Centre|location=Cambridge, England|isbn=9780900332982|page=491|edition=1st}}<!--|accessdate=16 March 2015--></ref> She married Dr. [[Bruce E. Maryanoff]] on May 15, 1971.<ref name=Marriage>{{cite web|title=Brief Biography for Dr. Bruce E. Maryanoff, Ph.D.|url=http://darwin.chem.villanova.edu/~bausch/ISCC/BEMbio.htm|accessdate=16 March 2015|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304072704/http://darwin.chem.villanova.edu/~bausch/ISCC/BEMbio.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Maryanoff received a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] degree in chemistry in 1972 from [[Drexel University]],<ref>{{citation|title=NCCE Co-op Hall of Fame Class of 2002–2003 |url=http://www.co-op.edu/NCCE%20assets/08BOC/site%20pdfs/boc_08_hof/24451_pg78-79.pdf |publisher=National Commission for Cooperative Education |accessdate=2009-05-03 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080705130845/http://www.co-op.edu/NCCE%20assets/08BOC/site%20pdfs/boc_08_hof/24451_pg78-79.pdf |archivedate=2008-07-05 }}{{full citation needed|date=March 2013}}</ref> and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degree in organic chemistry in 1976 from [[Princeton University]], working with [[Kurt Mislow]].<ref name=Arkivoc>{{cite journal|title=A Tribute to Dr. Cynthia A. Maryanoff|journal=Arkivoc|date=2010|volume=2010|issue=8|pages=6–9|doi=10.3998/ark.5550190.0011.802|url=http://www.arkat-usa.org/get-file/32373/|accessdate=16 March 2015|doi-access=free|last1=Waring|first1=Anthony|hdl=2027/spo.5550190.0011.802|hdl-access=free}}</ref> From 1976 to 1977 she was a postdoctoral fellow in the department of chemistry at Princeton University, working with [[Edward C. Taylor]].<ref name=Arkivoc/>

==Career==
She joined [[Smith, Kline & French]] Laboratories in 1977 and moved to [[McNeil Pharmaceutical]], a [[Johnson & Johnson]] subsidiary in 1981. She served as global head of chemical and pharmaceutical development in preclinical development from 2000 to 2004, which was responsible for moving new chemical entities from small-scale to large-scale chemical synthesis, for analytical methods, and establishing  oral formulations for early human studies. Maryanoff advanced through various Johnson & Johnson pharmaceutical units to the highest scientific position in the company.<ref name=Arkivoc/><ref name=Cohen/>

In 2004 she moved to [[Cordis (medical)]] Corporation, a Johnson & Johnson medical device unit, as a distinguished research fellow in the Cordis facility in [[Spring House, Pennsylvania|Spring House]], [[Pennsylvania]].<ref name=Arkivoc/>  She retired from Johnson & Johnson in 2013.<ref name=perkin2015/> She then became a Distinguished Professor at the Baruch S. Blumberg Institute (Doylestown, Pennsylvania).<ref name=ACSInternational>{{cite web|title=ACS International Center|url=http://www.acs.org/content/dam/acsorg/global/international-center/13-travel-award-liysf.pdf|accessdate=April 30, 2014}}</ref>

Maryanoff has been active in the fields of [[organic chemistry]] and [[materials science]].  Her publication record includes more than 100 scientific papers and several books.<ref name=SciLive/> She is listed as an inventor on 67 U.S. or European [[patents]], issued or pending.<ref name=SciLive/><ref name=Justia>{{cite web|title=Patents by Inventor Cynthia A. Maryanoff|url=http://patents.justia.com/inventor/cynthia-a-maryanoff|website=Justia Patents|accessdate=16 March 2015}}</ref>

Maryanoff emphasizes that accomplishments in [[process chemistry]] depend upon the work of teams of people who are involved in the research.<ref name=Cohen>{{cite journal|last1=Cohen|first1=Judy|title=2006 Successful Women in Chemistry Interview: Interview with Cynthia Maryanof|journal=Women Chemists|date=2006|volume=Fall/Winter|page=6|url=http://womenchemists.sites.acs.org/fall-winter_2006.pdf|accessdate=16 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170326011522/http://womenchemists.sites.acs.org/fall-winter_2006.pdf|archive-date=26 March 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=perkin2015/> As a scientist and group leader she has been influential in creating drug candidates for a variety of conditions, including [[antipsychotics]],<ref name=Abell>{{cite book|last1=Abell|first1=Andrew|title=Advances in amino acid mimetics and peptidomimetics|date=1997|publisher=JAI Press|location=Greenwich, Connecticut|isbn=9780762302000}}</ref> [[antiepileptics]],<ref name=perkin2015/> [[Antiviral drug|antiviral agents]], and treatments for [[cardiovascular disease]] and female reproductive diseases.<ref name=Arkivoc/> She has also worked on the [[transdermal]] delivery of narcotics, [[pulmonary surfactants]], endocrine function, and Cordis [[drug-eluting stent]]s.<ref name=Arkivoc/>  The more than 1,000 drug candidates she has been involved in developing include the anti-epileptic [[Topamax]], and an atypical analgesic, Ultram/[[Tramadol]], for treating pain.<ref name=SciLive>{{cite news|title=Cynthia A. Maryanoff to receive prestigious Perkin Medal|url=http://www.scientistlive.com/content/cynthia-maryanoff-receive-prestigious-perkin-medal|work=Scientist Live|date=14 April 2015}}</ref>

She has been active in the [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS) in many positions including national election to the Executive Committee of the Division of Organic Chemistry (DOC) (1988–2018).<ref name=ACSInternational/><ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-08-16 |title=Executive Committee - ACS Division of Organic Chemistry |url=https://www.organicdivision.org/executivecommittee/ |access-date=2022-08-22 |language=en-US}}</ref> She was the first woman to be chair of the Division of Organic Chemistry (DOC) (1997).<ref name=Arkivoc/>  She has served on a variety of other committees including the Advisory Board of [[Chemical & Engineering News]],<ref name=Arkivoc/> the International Activities Committee (2014-2022),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Committee on International Activities Roster |url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/about/governance/committees/international-activities/roster.html |access-date=2022-08-22 |website=American Chemical Society |language=en}}</ref> and the ACS Governing Board of Publishing (2015-2023).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Governing Board for Publishing |url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/about/governance/committees/governing-board-publishing.html |access-date=2022-08-22 |website=American Chemical Society |language=en}}</ref> As well as the ACS, she has been active on the NSF Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Review Panel, the NIH Division of Grants, and the NCI Committee for Proposals to Synthesize Pharmaceutical Agents.<ref name=Arkivoc/>

==Memberships and fellowships==
* member of the Philadelphia section of the American Chemical Society (ACS)<ref name=Arkivoc/>
* member of the Philadelphia Organic Chemists Club (POCC)<ref name=Arkivoc/>
* fellow of the American Institute of Chemists<ref name=Arkivoc/>
* fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science<ref name=Arkivoc/>
* fellow of the American Chemical Society (ACS):  She was one of 162 members chosen for the inaugural group of fellows.<ref name=Arkivoc/>

==Awards==
{{library resources box|by=yes|lcheading=Maryanoff, Cynthia A. }}
Maryanoff is the recipient of numerous awards, including the Philadelphia Section Award from [[American Chemical Society]] (1991); [[Garvan–Olin Medal]] from the American Chemical Society (1999); Philadelphia Organic Chemists' Club Award (1999); the Earle B. Barnes Award for Leadership in Chemical Research Management, a national award of the American Chemical Society (2005);<ref name=Barnes>{{cite web|title=Alumna Cynthia A. Maryanoff Wins an Award|url=http://drexel.edu/chemistry/news/archive/20050311/|website=Department of Chemistry|publisher=Drexel University|accessdate=March 11, 2005|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120120025101/http://drexel.edu/chemistry/news/archive/20050311/|archive-date=January 20, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> the Henry F. Whalen, Jr. Award for Business Development from the American Chemical Society Division of Business Development and Management (2007); the Anthony J. and Heand Silvestri Award (2008); and the Ronald Mitsch Award (2008). In 2003, she was inducted into the Drexel 100.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-22 |title=Awards and Recognition |url=https://drexel.edu/alumni/news-and-highlights/awards-and-recognition/drexel-100/biographies/inducted-2003/ |access-date=2022-08-22 |website=Alumni |language=en}}</ref> In 2010, she received the Elizabeth Bingham Award from the Philadelphia Chapter of the Association for Women in Science (AWIS-PHL), recognizing her contributions to the advancement of women in science.<ref name=AWSI2010>{{cite web|title=Elizabeth Bingham Award Winners|url=http://www.awisphl.org/Awardees.htm|website=AWIS Association for Women in Science|accessdate=16 March 2015|archive-date=2 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402100908/http://www.awisphl.org/Awardees.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> She and her husband [[Bruce E. Maryanoff]] are co-recipients of the 2015 Hepatitis B Foundation Community Commitment Award.<ref name=Hepatitis>{{cite news|title=Hepatitis B Foundation to Honor Drs. Bruce and Cyndie Maryanoff|url=https://www.prweb.com/releases/hepatitis_b_foundation_to_honor_drs_bruce_and_cyndie_maryanoff/prweb12582647.htm|access-date=5 May 2015|work=PR News|date=April 17, 2015}}</ref> In 2015 Cynthia Maryanoff  received the [[Perkin Medal]] for outstanding work in applied chemistry in the U.S.A.<ref name=perkin2015>{{cite news|last1=Wang|first1=Linda|title=2015 Perkin Medal To Cynthia Maryanoff|url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/93/web/2015/03/2015-Perkin-Medal-Cynthia-Maryanoff.html|accessdate=16 March 2015|work=Chemical & Engineering News|date=March 10, 2015}}</ref>  In 2018 Maryanoff received the Paul G. Gassman Distinguished Service Award from the Division of Organic Chemistry of the American Chemical Society.<ref name="ACS2018">{{cite web |title=Paul G. Gassman Distinguished Service Award |url=https://www.organicdivision.org/professional-awards/gassmanaward/ |website=American Chemical Society |date=25 August 2016 |accessdate=16 April 2019}}</ref><ref name="Stanzione">{{cite web |last1=Stanzione |first1=Robin |title=2018 Gassman Award to Cynthia A. Maryanoff |url=https://www.organicdivision.org/blog/2018/05/31/2018-gassman-award-to-cynthia-a-maryanoff/ |website=American Chemical Society |accessdate=16 April 2019|date=May 31, 2018}}</ref> Cynthia A Maryanoff received the 2022 Drexel Golden Dragon Society Award.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-22 |title=Awards and Recognition |url=https://drexel.edu/alumni/news-and-highlights/awards-and-recognition/ |access-date=2022-08-22 |website=Alumni |language=en}}</ref>
